options.label: European Public Health, Disease and Policy
options.labelReason: Epidemiology, infection and disease, health psychology, research methods and EU law and politics form the closest academic option.
options.concept: Study how disease and health risks are distributed and how public institutions respond. Combine epidemiology and biomedical science with health psychology, research methods, European law and policymaking.
progression: The biomedicine and law gateways precede dependent courses. Research methods and introductory statistics precede advanced evidence appraisal.

options.label: Health Behaviour, Psychology and Communication
options.labelReason: Health psychology, social behaviour, mental health and persuasive communication frame this related option.
options.concept: Study how social conditions and individual behaviour affect health. Combine health psychology, sociology, behavioural economics and communication to examine health messages and the choices people make.
options.distinctness: This option adds social and organisational psychology, mental health, behavioural economics and practical communication. The closest option gives greater weight to disease mechanisms, EU law and environmental governance.
traceOverrides: introduces epidemiology as the science of studying disease, risk and change over time and of evaluating evidence; in this programme it directly implements the epidemiological method with which behavioural and social risk factors are identified, and is the population-level anchor of the programme

teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis in R for evidence-based policy making; in this programme it directly implements the evidence-synthesis training used to appraise behavioural and communication interventions and is placed last as the research capstone

teaches how state and non-state interests are turned into policy, the institutions and decision-making rules of the EU; in this programme it directly implements the political process behind the policy-advocacy strand, without any health focus

follows human development across the lifespan, including ageing; in this programme it makes a specific complementary contribution to the psychological and social determinants of health over the life course

teaches persuasion strategies, framing, nudging and the ethics of persuasion beyond the humanities in communication studies and social psychology; in this programme it makes a specific complementary contribution to health communication and advocacy as the capstone of the rhetoric sequence, without health content

analysis: The closest plan applies epidemiological measures and study designs to population health. Infection & Immunity and Mechanisms of Disease contribute pathogen, immune and organ-system mechanisms, and Pharmacology contributes drug action and development. EU law and politics supply actual legal and institutional tools, while Public Economics contributes taxation, externalities and equity including healthcare and public spending. Research Methods & Statistics, experimental methods, qualitative inquiry and data science cover sampling, inference, interviewing and data visualisation. Advanced Research Methods adds a systematic review, not supervised placement research. Climate Change includes climate and health, justice and governance, and Governance of Sustainability contributes institutions and policy evaluation. The second plan concentrates on behaviour change, prevention, social influence, workplace health, mental health and public communication. Behavioural experiments, marketing research and applied rhetoric offer transferable evidence and advocacy tools rather than health-specific professional training. The plans differ by ten courses in each direction. Environmental sustainability, ecological processes and selected health risks are real overlaps, but there is insufficient sustained environmental exposure or environmental epidemiology for a third programme centred on health. Management courses can supply organisational practice but do not provide comparative healthcare finance, organisation and delivery as a sustained field. A research placement is a mode of study, not an additional academic direction.

alignment.rationale: Epidemiology & Public Health teaches epidemiology as the science of studying disease, risk and change over time and of evaluating evidence, the core of Demography and Epidemiology of Ageing and Migration (epidemiological concepts and methods, research designs, association measures, bias and causal interpretation); it lacks the demography, ageing and migration topics and the EU focus.
Both use descriptive and inferential statistics. UCR applies study design and statistical analysis in a team project.

Statistics & Experimental Methods covers multivariate models (regression, logistic regression, ANOVA) and experimental design, the statistical-analysis and study-design part of Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods (chi-square tests, t-tests, regression and trial designs); it does not cover programme evaluation or process evaluation.

Advanced Research Seminar teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis for evidence-based policy, the evidence-synthesis skill at the centre of the Year 1 literature-review paper (finding, interpreting and combining public-health evidence); it is a statistical synthesis course and does not teach academic writing.

Pharmacology covers drug origin, therapeutic use, toxicity and rational drug development, the pharmaceutical innovation strand of Health-Technological Innovation and EU Competencies; it does not cover medical devices, big data, safety assessment or the EU regulatory competencies.

Medical & Health Psychology covers the bio-psycho-social approach to health and illness, health-psychology theory and interventions, matching the individual health-behaviour and intervention content of Lifestyle, Work and Health in the EU; it does not cover work characteristics or EU lifestyle and occupational-health policy.

Foundations of European Union Law covers the EU institutional framework, legal order, fundamental rights and internal market, matching the EU history, treaties, institutions and legal-structures part of Health, Health Determinants and the European Union; it does not cover the concepts of health and public health, health determinants and health inequalities, which make up most of the component.

European Union Politics covers EU actors, institutions, decision-making rules and how interests are turned into policy, matching the multilevel EU policy-making, actors and advocacy of Health Policies at EU Level and Global Health Europe; it has no health-policy content or global-health dimension.

Public Economics covers market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, public spending and redistribution, matching the financing and market part of (Public) Health Care Systems in the EU; it does not cover health-system frameworks, insurance schemes or health-system reforms.

Climate Change covers the drivers and societal impacts of climate change, including effects on health, food and migration, matching the climate-change part of Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU; it does not cover air and water quality, built environments or the health-environment policy focus.
